mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future earnings, lowering the present value of equity expectations and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS level over the 60-day horizon (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and drives equity valuations higher over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in one month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In a labor strengthening regime, the 20-day forward return is not positively correlated with the combined PAYEMS/UNRATE interaction (Pearson's IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.2% inflation-adjusted growth for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports S&P 500 gains over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL grows at a monthly rate exceeding 0.2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 5-day realized return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in two consecutive months suggests supply-side shocks that reduce manufacturing capacity, leading to higher risk premia and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During supply shocks, the 20-day forward return shows no significant negative relationship with INDPRO (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, the central bank's policy rate normalization path is expected to slow, reducing the real discount rate and pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns into negative territory.
failure_condition: In regimes where FEDFUNDS is below 4% for > 30 days, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (HOUST) without a corresponding increase in layoffs (PAYEMS) indicate a tight labor market, which elevates wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for two consecutive months while PAYEMS remains flat or increases
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return shows no significant positive relationship with the HOUST/PAYEMS interaction (IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of declining consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 300) and rising real wage growth (unobserved proxy implied), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 20-day forward returns regardless of FEDFUNDS policy, due to optimism about real income.
failure_condition: In low-inflation regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 20-day realized return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time spike in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.5 percentage points, followed by a rapid decline back below the pre-spike level within a week, creates a 'flattened yield curve' signal that is associated with short-term equity volatility but not with sustained S&P 500 gains over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS spikes > 0.5pp and declines > 0.5pp within 7 trading days
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not significantly different from the 5-day realized return (p > 0.05) during such spikes.
